newsitem.title: UK: Dlr ends mixed in Europe, Dutch rate hike pondered.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends mixed in Europe, Dutch rate hike pondered.

text.p: The dollar closed mixed here but shrugged off a Dutch interest rate rise which initially raised concern whether the European easing cycle might be at an end.

The Dutch central bank raised its key special advances rate to 2.70 percent from 2.50. The dollar dipped initially to session lows. But analysts were quick to point out that the rise should be seen in connection with the country's strong economic performance compared to Germany and its higher inflation rate.
"You would have to be seriously paranoid to think the Dutch rate hike is a harbinger for European rates to go up," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro.
Dutch gross domestic product rose 2.8 percent year-on-year in the fourth quarter of 1996, data released on Thursday showed.
The Netherlands' inflation rate stood at 2.3 percent in January. German CPI, in comparison, is still below two percent and was at 1.8 percent in February.
The Dutch rate move followed a rise in money market rates and several days of guilder weakness. The guilder had slipped to its lowest level since April 1994 on Wednesday.
"Given the strong link between the guilder and the mark, the rise caused a bit of a stir but it didn't come unexpected, so the net effect was marginal," said a trader at a German bank.
At 1630 GMT, the dollar stood at 1.6885/95 marks and 120.72/80 yen, little changed from 1.6890/6900 in late European trading on Wednesday but down from 122.10/20.
Yen strength remained a key feature. The Japanese currency pushed the mark to an eight-month low of 71.41 yen, also weakening the dollar/yen rate.

Worries about profit-taking and fiscal year-end repatriation of funds in Japan are lifting the currency. Stronger-than-expected Japanese industrial production data overnight and the belief that dollar/yen will be capped by Japanese and U.S. authorities on any move over 125 yen have also boosted the yen.

Dollar/mark got a fresh boost, meantime, after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan warned on Wednesday about a possible pre-emptive U.S. interest rate rise. His comment pushed the 10-year bund/T-bond yield spread to more than 100 basis points in favour of T-bonds.
Comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer about EMU and the dollar had little net impact on trade, analysts said.
Tietmeyer painted a gloomy picture of the prospects for EMU if two key requirements, a stable single currency and lasting budget restraint, are not met.
Tietmeyer also said current exchange rates better reflected economic fundamentals on both sides of the Atlantic.
